title: Manual trip close
summary: Allow an organiser to confirm and permanently complete an active trip while preserving final balances and rejecting subsequent ledger writes.

specifications.summary: Finalise active trips only through an organiser-confirmed manual action.
specifications.details: The finalised ledger stays readable, but no contribution or expense can be added after completion.

acceptance.summary: An organiser can confirm ending an active trip.
Members can identify and read a completed trip and its final balances.
Contributions and expenses are rejected after a trip is completed.
Only the organiser can complete a trip, and only while it is active.

contexts.title: Trip lifecycle
contexts.summary: Owns a trip's draft, active, and completed states and the organiser authority to change state.

glossary.meaning: A final trip state in which its ledger remains readable but cannot accept new entries.

contexts.title: Shared ledger
contexts.summary: Owns contributions, expenses, allocations, and the rule that entries can be recorded only for active trips.

physicalBoundaries.title: TripMate application
physicalBoundaries.location: Next.js application and its Supabase-backed data access
physicalBoundaries.summary: Serves the browser UI and performs authenticated trip commands through the existing API route and database RPCs.

infrastructure.title: Next.js
infrastructure.responsibility: Renders the client interaction and dispatches authenticated API commands.
infrastructure.rationale: Existing application framework and request boundary.

infrastructure.title: Supabase RPC and PostgreSQL
infrastructure.responsibility: Persists trip status and enforces authorisation and ledger-state rules in database functions.
infrastructure.rationale: Existing authoritative persistence and access-control boundary.

models.title: Trip record
models.summary: Persisted trip identity, organiser, dates, cash holder, and lifecycle status.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Lifecycle state controlling whether ledger writes are permitted.

models.title: Complete trip request
models.summary: Authenticated command identifying the trip the organiser wants to complete.

fields.name: trip
fields.description: Trip to transition from active to completed.

workflows.title: Finalise a trip ledger
workflows.summary: An organiser closes a finished trip, members retain final-balance visibility, and later ledger writes are refused.
workflows.goal: Provide an intentional, final endpoint for shared-trip accounting without losing the completed ledger.
workflows.diagram: Organiser confirms completion → application stores completed state → members view final ledger; later ledger entry → rejected

actions.title: Complete an active trip
actions.summary: The organiser confirms the end-trip action and receives the saved completed state.
steps: Show the organiser-only End trip control for an active trip.
Ask the organiser to confirm that the ledger is final.
Validate the authenticated organiser and active trip state.
Persist the trip status as completed and refresh the snapshot.
businessRules: Only the organiser may complete a trip.
Only an active trip may be completed.
Completion is permanent in this version.

serviceRoles.description: Presents confirmation and executes the authenticated lifecycle transition.

infrastructureLinks.description: Shows the confirmed end-trip interaction and posts the command through the existing API route.
Uses a guarded database RPC to change the authoritative trip status.

modelLinks.description: Changes an active trip to completed.

actions.verification: Browser acceptance test covers the confirmed organiser path; database integration tests cover authority and active-state guards.

actions.title: View a completed ledger
actions.summary: A member sees the completed label, final entries, and calculated bill without any new-entry controls.
steps: Load the completed trip snapshot for a current member.
Display its completed state, ledger totals, and member bill.
Withhold controls that add funds or expenses.
businessRules: Completion preserves member read access to the final ledger.

serviceRoles.description: Renders the persisted final ledger to authorised members.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses the existing ledger view to communicate final status and balances.
Fetches the existing member-authorised trip snapshot.

modelLinks.description: Uses the completed status to choose the read-only ledger presentation.

actions.verification: Browser acceptance test proves the completed marker and final ledger remain visible.

actions.title: Reject a closed-trip ledger entry
actions.summary: A member attempting a contribution or expense after completion receives a rejected command and no ledger mutation.
steps: Receive a contribution or expense command for the trip.
Read the authoritative trip lifecycle state.
Reject the command when the trip is completed without creating ledger records.
businessRules: Funds and expenses may be recorded only while a trip is active.

serviceRoles.description: Forwards ledger commands to persistence, where lifecycle rules are enforced.

infrastructureLinks.description: Uses the contribution and expense RPC guards to reject writes for completed trips.
Runs PGlite-backed integration tests against the migration and RPC behavior.

modelLinks.description: Reads the persisted status as the write eligibility rule.

actions.verification: PGlite integration tests prove both contribution and expense RPCs fail after completion and create no rows.

edges.label: completed trip
edges.description: After status is saved, members can read the final ledger.

edges.label: completed state
edges.description: A later ledger command uses the completed state to determine rejection.

records.title: Trip lifecycle state
records.summary: The persisted status provides the finalisation state for display and command validation.

notes: The scheduled end date does not automatically complete a trip.

workflows.verification: Validate organiser completion, visible final ledger, non-organiser/state rejection, and frozen contribution and expense commands at their lowest appropriate test levels.

testCases.title: Organiser confirms completion from the active ledger
testCases.given: An organiser is viewing an active trip ledger.
testCases.then: The ledger refreshes as completed and no longer presents new-entry actions.

testCases.title: Non-organiser and non-active completion commands fail
testCases.given: A member or an organiser with a non-active trip sends the completion command.
testCases.when: The database RPC validates the command.
testCases.then: It returns an authorisation or lifecycle-state error without changing the trip record.

testCases.title: Completed trip remains readable to members
testCases.given: A member opens a completed trip.
testCases.then: The page labels the trip completed and shows its final ledger and bill.

testCases.title: Completed trips reject new contributions and expenses
testCases.when: A current member calls each ledger write RPC.
testCases.then: Both calls fail and no contribution, expense, or allocation is persisted.

testCases.title: Organiser authority permits the active-trip completion transition
testCases.given: The authenticated organiser owns an active trip.
testCases.then: The trip status is persisted as completed.

testCases.title: Active trips continue accepting valid ledger entries
testCases.given: A trip is active and a current member submits valid ledger commands.
testCases.when: The contribution and expense RPCs validate their lifecycle state.

choices: Selected: manual organiser-only completion with confirmation rather than automatic closure on the scheduled end date.
Selected: server-side RPC guards remain authoritative for both the completion transition and post-completion write rejection.
Excluded: reopening completed trips, settlement payments, and notifications.
constraints: Reuse the existing Next.js client, API route, Supabase RPC, and PostgreSQL migration architecture.
Preserve draft and active behaviours while adding completed as a final lifecycle state.
Existing invitations remain unchanged because they do not write ledger entries.
